chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah and Ibn Muskann, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman during her waiting period. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are separated, and if he had consummated the marriage with her, she is entitled to the dower corresponding to what she permitted of her private part, and they are separated so she is not permissible for him ever; and if he had not consummated the marriage with her, then she has nothing from her dower.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man marrying a woman during her waiting period?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the ruling for a marriage contracted during the waiting period (iddah) of a previous union, establishing that consummation results in permanent prohibition (ghair mubah) and full dower, while non-consummation yields no dower. It highlights the juristic distinction between the validity of the contract and the permanence of the bond based on physical intimacy, a key topic in Shia fiqh regarding 'iddah and dower distribution.
